subsystems.name: Optical terminal
subsystems.role: sends or receives the actual signal through the lens; the Sun's 1.4 million km width sets an enormous effective aperture, so even a modest telescope can be collimated to a very narrow beam.

subsystems.name: Beamline (the Sun as lens)
subsystems.role: the lens itself — not hardware, but a geometry that must be modelled and exploited, with the solar disc blocking the line of sight unless occulted.

subsystems.name: Station-keeping and navigation
subsystems.role: holds the terminal on the anti-stellar axis, where lateral excursions of even a few kilometres degrade the gain.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: sunlight is negligible past 550 AU, so the terminal needs its own reactor or radioisotope source.

subsystems.name: Relay and backhaul
subsystems.role: the terminal must talk to Earth across 550 AU while simultaneously pointing at a distant star, so a separate high-power link is needed.

subsystems.name: Delivery and propulsion
subsystems.role: getting mass to the focal region in decades rather than centuries.
parts: solar flyby heat shield for an Oberth manoeuvre

buildSteps.title: Fix the geometry
buildSteps.detail: Choose the target star, then compute the narrow anti-stellar line where the Sun focuses its light; the useful lateral offset from that line is small, so the operating point must be defined before any hardware is built.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical terminal
buildSteps.detail: Work out aperture, wavelength and transmit power needed to close the link against the Sun's own brightness and coronal noise, and whether a coronagraph is required to hide the solar disc.

buildSteps.title: Build the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Assemble telescope, laser, reactor, radiators, thrusters and an ultra-stable clock into a package light enough to launch and hardy enough to survive a close solar pass.

buildSteps.title: Launch and dive past the Sun
buildSteps.detail: Fly a heat-shielded probe very close to the Sun, where a small burn buys a large velocity change, converting a centuries-long cruise into roughly two to three decades.

buildSteps.title: Cruise
buildSteps.detail: Spend 20 to 30 years coasting outward with periodic ranging and autonomous navigation, keeping the spacecraft healthy and its clock stable.

buildSteps.title: Arrive and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Use known background radio sources and stars to find the exact focal line; the corona distorts the lens, so the terminal must map and correct for that noise before it is useful.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the terminal
buildSteps.detail: Point the optics at the target star and separately establish a high-power optical link back toward the inner solar system.

buildSteps.title: Operate
buildSteps.detail: Send the coded signal; reception at the far end would require a counterpart station sitting on that star's own focal line, built to the same principles.

prerequisites.why: laser links have been demonstrated across hundreds of millions of kilometres, but not across hundreds of astronomical units.
solar panels are useless at 550 AU; reactors have been ground-tested but not flown for this kind of decades-long mission.
at Voyager-like speeds the trip takes many centuries, so a close solar flyby, nuclear-electric stage or beamed sail is essential.
coherent detection over these distances demands oscillators that drift very little over years.
the bending is well understood, but coronal turbulence and noise must be characterised before gain can be realised.

pathway.milestone: theory and mission-concept studies, mostly aimed at using the lens to image exoplanets rather than to transmit
pathway.unlocks: a quantitative link budget showing what a terminal would need.

pathway.milestone: a small robotic precursor reaches the focal region with a telescope and measures the lens and its noise directly
pathway.unlocks: real data on gain and turbulence instead of models.

pathway.milestone: a relay chain of high-power optical links between the focal region and Earth
pathway.unlocks: a genuine transmit-and-receive station rather than a one-way beacon.

pathway.milestone: a deliberate transmission to a nearby star, and a two-way link if a counterpart station is built there
pathway.unlocks: interstellar communication at data rates no ordinary transmitter could reach.
